drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: Opening item. A health insurer's claims team revises its extraction prompt. The eval suite passes
drills.answer_line: SAM: The answer is B. The trigger was a prompt change
drills.stem: A health insurer's claims team revises its extraction prompt. The eval suite passes at 99%. A week later, adjusters report missing incident dates on scanned, partly handwritten forms. The model version is pinned and latency hasn't moved. Most likely root cause?

options.A: The model's behaviour changed under the pinned version
options.B: The golden dataset predates the prompt change and holds few or no scanned, handwritten forms
options.C: The judge model grading the extractions is too lenient

drills.why: The trigger was a prompt change; the suite kept passing because the golden dataset predates it and lacks the failing input class. Pinning rules out A.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A retailer's returns assistant reads an order
drills.answer_line: ALEX: A and C. A is a known-value comparison. C is the identifier scan.
drills.stem: A retailer's returns assistant reads an order, approves or routes the return, and drafts a reply. Which two checks should be code-based?

options.A: The refund amount in the reply matches the order system
options.B: The reply's tone is empathetic and on-brand
options.C: The reply contains no order number belonging to another customer
options.D: The reply correctly captures why the customer is returning the item
options.E: Escalation was the right call on an ambiguous, partly damaged item

drills.why: A is a known-value comparison and C is an identifier scan, both deterministic. Tone and meaning go to a judge; the ambiguous escalation is judge or human territory.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A state benefits agency tests a revised prompt on its eligibility
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. A treats noise as signal; it's the underpowered-test distractor
drills.stem: A state benefits agency tests a revised prompt on its eligibility chatbot. 60 sessions per version give task success of 71% against 64%. The product owner wants to ship today. Best next step?

options.B: Pre-specify metrics, calculate sample size, assign sessions randomly and consistently, run to that size
options.C: Move to a more capable model first
options.D: Keep the test running and stop as soon as the gap reaches significance

drills.why: 60 a side is a confirmation check, not a test. A treats noise as signal, C changes a different variable, and D runs until you see what you want.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A retailer's product assistant tells a customer a blender
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Retrieval worked, so it isn't rag. The model asserted something
drills.stem: A retailer's product assistant tells a customer a blender has a 5-year warranty. The trace shows the right product page was retrieved, and it says 2 years. Best fix?

options.A: Add "never make up warranty terms" to the system prompt
options.B: Move to the most capable tier
options.C: Require each warranty claim to cite a retrieved passage and verify the term against it before replying

drills.why: Retrieval worked; the model asserted something not in its context. That is hallucination, and grounding plus verification removes it at the root.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A field service dispatch assistant takes sixty thousand
drills.answer_line: SAM: Right. A attacks the dominant input cost and helps latency.
drills.stem: A dispatch assistant takes 60,000 calls a month with a 6,000-token system prompt that rarely changes. It's over its cost ceiling with a tight latency target, and makes nightly work-order summaries needed by morning. Which two changes close the gap without losing required content?

options.A: Put the stable system prompt first, volatile content after, and enable prompt caching
options.C: Move every call to the most capable tier
options.D: Send the nightly summaries through the Batch API
options.E: Cut the system prompt in half

drills.why: A attacks the dominant input cost and helps latency; D moves work that can wait onto discounted pricing. E is the blunt cut that loses required content.
